question: What is MBKTech.org?
answer: MBKTech.org is a collaborative development studio founded by Muhammad Bin Khalid. We specialize in open-source software development, web and mobile applications, and innovative technology solutions. Our mission is to create impactful digital tools that benefit the global tech community through collaboration and open-source contributions.

question: Who is behind MBK Tech?
answer: MBK Tech was founded by Muhammad Bin Khalid and operates as a two-person team alongside collaborator Maaz Waheed (specializing in AI and Data Science). Together, we build and maintain all projects, write documentation, and provide support to our users and clients.

question: What makes MBK Tech different from other development studios?
answer: We focus heavily on open-source contributions and community-driven development. Every project we build is designed to be transparent, well-documented, and reusable. We also prioritize direct communication with our clients — no account managers, no bureaucracy — you talk directly to the developers building your project.

question: What services does MBK Tech offer?
answer: We offer a range of professional technology services including Web Development (frontend and full-stack), Custom Software Development, Technical Consulting, and Maintenance & Support. For a complete overview with package details, visit our Services page.

question: What technologies do you work with?
answer: Our core stack includes HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Node.js, React, PostgreSQL, and Python. We also have experience with AWS, Vercel, Linux, C++, and various CI/CD tools. We choose the right technology for each project rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all approach.

question: Do you provide ongoing maintenance after a project is delivered?
answer: Yes. We offer maintenance and support plans for all projects we build. This includes bug fixes, security updates, performance monitoring, and feature enhancements. Maintenance packages start at affordable monthly rates — see our Services page for details.

question: How long does a typical project take?
answer: Timelines depend on the project scope and complexity. A basic website typically takes 1–2 weeks, while a full-stack web application may take 3–6 weeks. After an initial consultation, we provide a detailed timeline estimate tailored to your requirements.

question: How can I contact MBK Tech?
answer: The best way to reach us is through our Support & Contact page. You can submit a support ticket, send feedback, request a quote, or make a general inquiry — all from one form. You can also email us directly at support@mbktech.org.

question: How do I track my support ticket?
answer: When you submit a support request, you receive a unique ticket number (e.g., T000123456). Use this number on our Track Ticket page to check the status, view updates, and see the full audit trail of your request at any time.

question: What is your typical response time?
answer: We aim to respond to all inquiries within 24–48 hours. Support tickets are prioritized by urgency, and we provide status updates throughout the resolution process. For time-sensitive issues, please include as much detail as possible in your initial message.

question: What should I include in my support request?
answer:
To help us resolve your issue quickly, please include:
  • A clear description of the issue or request
  • The relevant project or service name
  • Steps to reproduce (for bugs)
  • Screenshots or error messages (if applicable)
  • Your preferred contact method

question: How can I collaborate with MBK Tech?
answer: We welcome collaboration on open-source projects, technical content, and community initiatives. Use the Collaboration option on our Contact form to pitch your idea. We review every proposal and respond within a few days.

question: Do you accept open-source contributions?
answer: Absolutely. Our projects are open-source and hosted on GitHub. You can contribute by submitting pull requests, reporting bugs, improving documentation, or suggesting features. Check individual project repositories for contribution guidelines.
